header.description: The header segments to draw, in drawing order; a segment left out is hidden, and an empty list hides the header.

rows.description: The rows to draw below the header, in drawing order; a row left out is hidden, and an empty list hides every row.

mode.description: How the statusline is laid out: expanded draws the header and then the rows, each on lines of its own as layout.merge allows, and compact draws the header segments and every row's content on one line, starting a new line only where the line would be wider than the width. layout.mergeBars, layout.merge, layout.rightAlign and layout.rule have no effect in compact.

rule.description: Whether a rule is drawn across the line between the header and the rows beneath it, as wide as the header's widest line (at least twenty columns, at most the width); it is drawn only when both the header and the rows have something to show, and not in the compact layout.

mergeBars.description: Whether bar rows that sit next to each other in layout.rows share a line, and one grid, when they fit (the context and quota bars do by default); when false each bar row is on a line of its own, its bars still aligned to its neighbours'. A row of text is never joined by this setting, whichever form the quota row takes: layout.merge does that.

merge.description: Groups of rows that share a line when they sit next to each other in layout.rows and fit on one line together, and are drawn on lines of their own when they do not; each group names at least two rows, and no row belongs to two groups. A group may mix bar rows and rows of text, which are joined with the separator when every member is a single line. Bar rows outside a group follow layout.mergeBars.

rightAlign.description: Rows that start the right-aligned part of a merged line: the first of them to appear on a line, and the rows after it, are pushed to the right edge, with the gap padded by spaces. A row named here must belong to a group in layout.merge, and it has no effect when it is the first row of its line.

maxWidth.description: The width in columns to draw for when the client reports none and the COLUMNS environment variable names none, in place of the 80 it would otherwise assume; 0 leaves it at that.

forceMaxWidth.description: Whether maxWidth is the width drawn for whatever the client reports, even when the terminal is narrower or wider; it needs maxWidth to be set.

format.description: How the model's name is written: full is the name as the client gives it, compact drops a context-window suffix such as (1M context), and short also drops a leading Claude.

override.description: A name to show in place of the client's own model name, whatever model is running; empty shows the model's own name. A dynamic mode's served model still follows it.

source.description: Where the model's name comes from: client is the name the client reports, transcript is the model the session's last reply came from (what a proxy actually served), and auto uses the transcript's model only when it is not a Claude model, which is what a proxy redirect looks like.

name.description: A label to show in place of the launch's provider name, or on its own when the launch has no provider; empty shows the provider's own name.

parts.description: What the account segment says about the login account, in drawing order: the account's email address, its organisation (shown for team and enterprise accounts) and its plan. A part left out is hidden, and an empty list hides the segment.

userLength.description: The most characters of the account's email address to show, with an ellipsis after a cut one; 0 shows all of it.

format.description: How the reasoning effort is written: full is a symbol and the level (a filled circle that grows with the level, then the name), symbol is the symbol alone, and text is the level's name alone. A level with no symbol is always written as its name.

override.description: A name to show for the advisor model in place of the one the session's transcript records; empty shows the transcript's, prettified.

bar.description: Whether the context row draws its bar, or only its figures on one line of text.

value.description: The context figure: both (the tokens held against the window, then the percentage), percent, tokens, or remaining (the percentage of the window left).

warnAt.description: The whole percentage of the context window at which the context bar turns yellow; while it is unset the context bar follows bands.warnAt. A layer may write null to return it to unset when a shallower layer sets it.

criticalAt.description: The whole percentage of the context window at which the context bar turns red and, with context.breakdown set to critical, the token breakdown appears; while it is unset the context bar follows bands.criticalAt. A layer may write null to return it to unset when a shallower layer sets it.

autoCompactWindow.description: A window in tokens to measure the context against instead of the model's, matching the figure /context gives once Claude Code compacts before the window is full. While it is set, the row draws nothing until the client reports the tokens held, since without them there is nothing to measure against it; while it is unset the model's own window is used. A layer may write null to return it to unset when a shallower layer sets it.

estimate.description: What to draw when the client reports no percentage of the window in use, or reports 0 while tokens are already held (which is how a client says it has not worked it out yet): never (nothing is estimated: a percentage reported, 0 included, is drawn as it is, and none reported draws nothing), raw (the tokens held over the window), or buffered (that, plus the 16.5% of the window Claude Code reserves for compaction, rising from nothing at 5% of the window held to the whole reserve at 50%).

breakdown.description: Whether to add the input and cache tokens of the last request to the context row once its use reaches context.criticalAt.

warnAt.description: The whole percentage of use at which a bar turns yellow; it must be below criticalAt.

criticalAt.description: The whole percentage of use at which a bar turns red.

fiveHour.description: The name of the five-hour subscription window.

sevenDay.description: The name of the weekly subscription window.

width.description: A bar's width in cells before the line's spare width is shared out among the bars.

filled.description: The character that draws the used part of a bar.

empty.description: The character that draws the unused part of a bar.

value.description: Whether a quota window's figure is the share of it used or the share left; the bar and the colour always follow the share used.

bar.description: Whether each quota window is drawn as a bar, or as text alone.

compact.description: Whether the quota windows are drawn as one short line of text (`5h: 25.0% (1h 30m)`) in place of bars; it takes precedence over usage.bar.

resetLabel.description: Whether a window's reset time is introduced with `resets in` (`resets` for a wall-clock time), as in `(resets in 1h 30m)`, rather than the bare `(1h 30m)`.

modelScoped.description: Whether the per-model weekly windows the client reports (rate_limits.model_scoped) are drawn after the account's own windows; they describe the signed-in account, so a session that selected a provider never shows them.

timeFormat.description: How a window's reset is shown: the time left (`1h 30m`), the wall-clock time (`at 14:30`), both, the share of the window already gone (`53% elapsed`), or that share and the wall-clock time. A window whose length is not known shows no share.

threshold.description: The whole percentage of use that at least one quota window must reach for the quota row to be drawn at all; 0 always draws it.

sevenDayThreshold.description: The whole percentage of use at which the weekly window is drawn beside the five-hour one; below it the weekly window is hidden. A weekly window with no five-hour window beside it is always drawn, and 0 always draws it.

hourCycle.description: The hour cycle of a wall-clock time: `auto` follows the system locale, `h23` and `h24` are 24-hour time (`h24` writes midnight as 24:00), and `h12` and `h11` are 12-hour time with am or pm (`h11` writes the hour after midnight as 0).

seconds.description: Whether a wall-clock time includes seconds (`14:30:07`).

routed.description: Whether the cost segments draw for a session routed through a provider or a cloud platform's model id, where the client's own figure is not what was billed; the figure drawn is then priced from the door's usage log with `agent-shim model price`, else the client's own when it is above zero.

threshold.description: The fewest configuration items in total (CLAUDE.md files, rules, MCP servers and hook events) that must exist for the environment row to draw its counts.

parts.description: The parts of the sessionTime row to draw, in drawing order: when the session started, and how long ago the last response was written; a part left out is hidden, and an empty list hides the row.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the prompt cache lives, in seconds, when the transcript has not yet shown which tier the session writes (five minutes or one hour); the tier the transcript shows takes over once it does.

context.description: The colour of the context bar and its figures below the warning threshold.

usage.description: The colour of the quota bars and their figures below the warning threshold.

warning.description: The colour of the context bar at or above bands.warnAt, and of a cache hit share that is middling.

usageWarning.description: The colour of a quota bar at or above bands.warnAt.

critical.description: The colour of a bar at or above bands.criticalAt, and of a cache hit share that is nearly nothing.

model.description: The colour of the model and provider segments.

label.description: The colour of labels and secondary text: row labels, and the route, account, identity and headroom segments.

empty.description: The colour of the unused part of a bar.

project.description: The colour of the project path segment.

git.description: The colour of the version control segment's wrapper text (`git:(` and `)`).

gitBranch.description: The colour of the branch or bookmark and its ahead, behind and dirty markers.

pathLevels.description: How many trailing directories of the working directory the project segment shows: 1, 2 or 3, or full for the whole absolute path.

addedDirsLayout.description: Where the directories added to the session are drawn: inline, as +name after the project path in the project segment, or row, as an Added dirs line when layout.rows lists addedDirs.

enabled.description: Whether the vcs segment and the gitFiles row read the working directory's git status.

showDirty.description: Whether the branch is followed by * when the working tree has uncommitted changes.

showAheadBehind.description: Whether the branch is followed by the commits ahead of (up-arrow) and behind (down-arrow) its upstream.

showLineDiff.description: Whether the segment shows the total lines added and removed against HEAD, as [+a -d].

branchOverflow.description: How the vcs segment sits beside the project segment when they are listed next to each other: truncate keeps them as one unit the client cuts off at the terminal's edge, and wrap lets the line break between them.

pushWarnAt.description: The count of unpushed commits at which the ahead marker takes colours.warning; 0 turns it off.

pushCriticalAt.description: The count of unpushed commits at which the ahead marker takes colours.critical; 0 turns it off.

enabled.description: Whether the vcs segment reads a Jujutsu repository's status, instead of git's, when the working directory is inside one.

showDirty.description: Whether the bookmark or change id is followed by * when the working-copy commit differs from its parent.

showConflicts.description: Whether the segment shows !conflict when the working-copy commit has an unresolved conflict.
